 Gold Spot / U.S. Dollar Education 14 hours ago Gold: A level needs an expiry date
 0 Grab this chart 61 A price level can remain visible after the reasoning behind it has expired. This tutorial adds a time limit to chart analysis so that an old observation is not turned into a fresh signal after the outcome is known. 
 Chart context: OANDA:XAUUSD, 1 hour, viewed on TradingView on 30 October 2026 at 10:28 UTC (6:28 a.m. EDT). The displayed last price was 3982.125 at 10:28:34 UTC. This was an intrabar snapshot, not a completed H1 close or an executable entry quote. Broker feeds and spreads differ. No current support, resistance or trade setup is being validated here. 
 1. Structure can expire before a line disappears 
 A newer swing can change the context of an earlier range. Repeatedly drawing the same level does not establish that the original thesis still applies. The first blue annotation is a reminder to rebuild the structure assessment before forming a new thesis. The chart is background context for the method, not a marked live range. 
 2. A time window makes the claim testable 
 For a practice exercise, define a completed range and its boundaries on one feed and timeframe before reviewing what follows. Then observe the next three completed H1 candles. Three candles is an illustrative research rule, not an optimized or proven setting. 
 Confirmation: a completed close outside that predefined range followed by a retest that holds provides evidence of acceptance. Do not count a wick alone as a completed close or assume a retest has happened. 
 Failure: a close back inside weakens acceptance. Loss of the subsequently established holding-retest swing invalidates that interpretation. If the close-and-retest sequence is incomplete by the end of the three-candle window, record unconfirmed and reassess. Do not extend the window retrospectively to manufacture a successful call. 
 Validity: this is a reusable tutorial, not an active market forecast. Any exercise ends after its three completed H1 candles, or sooner if structure changes. It does not activate a new three-hour trade window from this publication. 
 Event check: the official U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics October calendar, checked today, schedules Q3 2026 Employment Cost Index for 30 October at 8:30 a.m. Eastern. No result or market reaction is assumed. A fresh market thesis should be reassessed around scheduled releases. Source: BLS, Schedule of Selected Releases for October 2026. 
 Previous tutorial review: the 29 October idea was explicitly reviewed at 6:12 a.m. EDT. Neither confirmation sequence completed within its original three-candle window. Later price movement does not retroactively convert that expired lesson into a confirmed trade or profit. 
 A useful journal has room for confirmed, invalidated and unconfirmed observations. Which do you record more consistently: the price condition or the deadline?
